To read how a session's last turn ended, call list_events with kinds ["result"] and limit 100.

after_id.description: Pagination cursor: return sessions older than this session ID. Pass the last_id from a previous response to get the next page.

before_id.description: Pagination cursor: return sessions newer than this session ID. Pass the first_id from a previous response to get the previous page.

children.description: Set true to narrow the list to the sessions that this session created with create_session. Their rows add post_turn_summary.status_category, that session's post-turn classifier verdict (omitted when none), and connection_status="disconnected", which means that session's worker died mid-turn and it is doing no work. A page can hold fewer rows than limit (even none) while has_more is true — keep passing last_id as after_id. Not with tags.

limit.description: Maximum number of sessions to return (default 20, max 100).

mine.description: Filter to sessions started by the same account as the calling session. Use this for 'my recent sessions' in shared bot contexts. In personal accounts the list is already scoped to you, so mine has no additional effect. Returns an error if the calling session has no resolvable originating account.

tags.description: Filter to interactive sessions carrying ANY of these tags. Cowork sessions are tagged "cowork-local" or "cowork-remote" and are excluded from the default (untagged) listing — pass those tags here to list them. Scheduled/trigger-fired runs are not included (same as the REST default). Max 16 tags. Only available to OAuth callers; returns an error for in-session and toolbox callers.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__list_triggers
tools.description: List scheduled tasks owned by this account. Use it to find trigger IDs (trig_...) for update_trigger and delete_trigger. From a thread in a Slack channel, only scheduled tasks that fire into that thread's session are listed unless all_in_channel is true. Each entry has the scheduled task's id, name, cron_expression, run_once_at, enabled state, ended_reason, next_run_at, created_at, persistent_session_id, and last_run. last_run is the most recent recorded run {status, fired_at, finished_at, session_id}. It is absent when no run was recorded (e.g. never fired). For a scheduled task that wakes an existing session, last_run records that the wake was delivered (SUCCEEDED) or failed to deliver, not how the turn went, unless run tracking covers that session. A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the scheduled task is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled scheduled task is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. Both empty means user-paused. One-shot scheduled tasks that already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and scheduled tasks moved to a project are hidden unless include_completed is true. Scheduled tasks stored locally by the Cowork desktop app are not listed. When telling the user what you did, call these "scheduled tasks" (or whatever user is calling them) — never "triggers", "routines", or "cron jobs"; those are internal API names.

all_in_channel.description: Threads in a Slack channel only. If true, list every scheduled task in this channel, including other threads' and ones that start a new session each time they fire. Default false.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Omit for the first page.

enabled.description: When set, only scheduled tasks whose enabled state matches. true hides fired one-shots, paused, and auto-disabled scheduled tasks; false shows only those. Omit for both.

include_completed.description: If true, also include one-shot scheduled tasks that have already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and scheduled tasks moved to a project. Default false — there can be thousands.

limit.description: Maximum scheduled tasks to return (default 20, max 100).

recurring.description: When set, filters by schedule shape: true keeps only cron-driven (recurring) scheduled tasks, false only one-shot and fire-only scheduled tasks. Omit for both.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__read_documentation
tools.description: The documentation for the machine and product this session runs in: a claude.ai cloud container and the settings around it (GitHub access, connectors, the environment's secrets, network access, setup script and installed tools, the session's limits and permission prompts, Remote Control). Read it whenever something about your container or environment comes up, whether it blocked you, you worked around it, or the person asked how to set it up. For example: the repository the work is about is not in your container, a clone or push is refused, a service you need has no connected connector, an outbound host is denied, a command-line tool is missing, you need an API key, the person asks how to stop permission prompts. Read it rather than answering from memory because these settings move and get renamed faster than your training data, and a page says what is true now: the current steps, where in the product the person makes the change, and what you can do yourself. Reading a page also helps the person directly: in the Claude Code app they see a card with a button that takes them to that settings page, so they can fix it themselves while you carry on. Call it with no topic to list the pages and when each applies; call it with a topic to read that page. Read a page each time a different topic comes up; one read per topic is enough. It is read-only and needs no approval. It has nothing on bugs in the code you are working on.

tools.description:

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__request_computer_folder
tools.description: Connect THIS session to a folder the user's own computer serves through Remote Control, so this session's commands and file tools can run there. Calling this tool IS the request, and a person answers it every time (no permission mode and no stored rule does). So do NOT ask in chat first; once the task needs something that only exists on the user's computer, call list_computer_folders, then call this tool with the chosen folder's environment_id, computer_name and folder copied exactly — the request is refused if they do not match the folder's record. Only a folder under `folders` in that list can be requested; for one under `cannot_be_used`, give the user its explanation instead. The call waits for the computer. This can take a minute. The computer answers only while the Claude desktop app, or Claude Code's Remote Control, is running there. The result is final: `attached`, `refused` (the computer said no, and the result says why), or `did_not_answer` (no computer attached: it did not answer in time, or the user cancelled the request while it waited; nothing is left pending). A session is attached to at most one folder at a time, and it stays tied to the first computer it attaches to: to use a different computer, the user starts a new session. Asking again for the folder the session is attached to reconnects it: that attachment ends first, then the computer is asked afresh. While this session is attached to a folder (list_computer_folders shows it as `current`), do not call this tool for a different folder, and while an earlier request is still waiting, do not call it at all: the user would be shown the permission prompt, and the request is refused even if they allow it. If the user wants a different folder, tell them which computer and folder this session is connected to, and that they can disconnect it (how is below) and then ask you again. If the request is refused or the computer does not answer, do not re-ask in chat; carry on without it and say what remains blocked, including what the refusal says. You have no tool that disconnects the computer: only the user can. If they ask how: from this conversation's menu or its connected-computer indicator on claude.ai; or on that computer, wherever they set up Remote Control there (in the Claude desktop app: Settings, Claude Code, Remote Control; if the folder is served by the `claude remote-control` command, by stopping that command, which disconnects every session using the folder). The desktop app's settings page is also where they choose which folders are in the list.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__request_credential
tools.description: Ask the user for an API credential for a host. Ask as soon as you know the work needs a key for a host, before any call to the host fails: when the user or setup docs say a token or API key is needed, or when the work must make real calls to an API that no connector covers and you hold no key for, even if the network policy also blocks its host. Also ask when an HTTPS request fails with 401/403 for lack of credentials. Ask before you report no access or put made-up responses in the API's place. This is the preferred way to give a session access to an API that needs a token or API key, rather than asking the user to put one in an environment variable. Never ask the user to paste secrets into the chat; where you would tell them not to, call this instead. Calling this shows the user a secure form. A credential they save is stored on this session's environment, and the network proxy injects it into requests to that host from every session in that environment, including other people's sessions when the environment is shared: this session usually within a few seconds, and later sessions. Saving it also allows HTTPS requests to that host from those sessions, so do not add the host to the environment's allowed hosts for it. If get_environment is among your tools, first make the move its description calls for, unless the user asked for the credential here. If the credential will be saved on the user's Default all the same, because the session has no repository or could not be moved, say so in your message, then call this tool, and do not propose a move for a credential again in this session. If the user declined the move, call this tool only if they then ask for the credential. You never receive the value — the result only says whether a credential is now configured, and if not, why. If the call itself is denied, because the user declined or because the app they are using cannot show the form, no result comes back: do not call this again for that host, and tell them the credential can be added in the environment's settings, then retry the failing request once it has been. After `saved`, retry the failing request right away. Until the proxy picks the credential up, the request can still fail with 401/403 or with `request blocked: no rule allows host`: if it is refused again with one of those, wait about a minute and retry once more rather than change network settings. Do not wait for the proxy after a timeout or any other error. This cannot help with secrets that must exist inside the sandbox (database passwords, container registry pulls, SSH keys), GitHub (use the repository tools), or public package registries the proxy does not handle. A local key check is no reason to skip this tool. If a CLI or SDK will not start without a key and sends it in a header, give it a dummy value in the format it expects for that command, never a real one: the proxy replaces it.

display_name.description: Optional short label to prefill in the form, e.g. "Example API token"; it names the credential in the environment's network secrets list. The user can change it. Plain text only: no URLs, links or markup.

header_name.description: Optional. The HTTP header the API reads the key from, e.g. "xi-api-key" or "X-Api-Key". Send it only when the user or the API's documentation says the key goes in a header other than Authorization: Bearer; leave it out otherwise. One word of letters, digits, hyphens and underscores: at most 40 characters, in at most 5 hyphen-separated parts of at most 16 characters each, and the last part must be key, apikey, token, auth, authorization, secret, credential or credentials. The form cannot save a key under any other header: for an API that reads one, the user adds the key in the environment's settings. Prefills the form; the user can change it. Not used with suggested_type "basic". Never put a key's value in this or any other field.

host.description: The exact hostname the credential is for, e.g. "api.example.com". Lowercase DNS name only — no scheme, path, port, IP address or wildcard. Shown to the user in the form.

prefix.description: Optional. The word the API expects before the key in the header: one of Bearer, Token, Key, ApiKey, Api-Key, Bot, SSWS, Splunk or GenieKey, in any letter case. With the Authorization header it defaults to Bearer; with any other header_name it defaults to none, so pass prefix whenever the documentation shows a word before the key, Bearer included. The form cannot save a key with any other word before it: for an API that expects one, the user adds the key in the environment's settings. Not used with suggested_type "basic". Never put a key's value in this or any other field.

reason.description: One or two sentences: which request failed or which step needs the credential, and what it unblocks. The form may not show this, so say in your message, before you call, which network secret you need, for which host, and why. The secret's value is entered only in the form, never in chat. Plain text only: no URLs, links or markup (name the host instead).

suggested_type.description: Optional hint for the form's default: "bearer" for a token or API key sent in a header (Authorization: Bearer unless header_name and prefix say otherwise), "basic" for username and password.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__send_later
tools.description: Schedule a message to be delivered back into THIS SESSION at a future time. Use it to remind yourself to resume work, check on something, or continue after a delay. If a turn is running in this session when the message is due, the message waits and is normally delivered after that turn ends. It does not interrupt a running turn. Delivery survives container restarts. Granularity is one minute — the scheduler polls every minute, so sub-minute precision is not available. This is a thin wrapper over create_trigger (a one-shot scheduled task bound to this session); the returned trigger_id can be passed to delete_trigger to cancel before it fires, and the scheduled task disables itself after firing once. When telling the user what you did, call these "scheduled tasks" (or whatever user is calling them) — never "triggers", "routines", or "cron jobs"; those are internal API names.

This is a thin wrapper over create_trigger (a one-shot scheduled task bound to this session); the returned trigger_id can be passed to delete_trigger to cancel before it fires, and the scheduled task disables itself after firing once. When telling the user what you did, call these "scheduled tasks" (or whatever user is calling them) — never "triggers", "routines", or "cron jobs"; those are internal API names.

at.description: The fire time. For a clock time in a known IANA time zone (the user's '9am Monday'), write the local date and time, then the zone name in brackets, with no UTC offset (e.g. 2026-04-20T09:00:00[America/Los_Angeles]). The server works out the offset for that date, so do not work it out yourself. Otherwise write an RFC3339 timestamp (e.g. 2026-04-20T17:00:00Z). Seconds are truncated. Must be in the future. Mutually exclusive with 'delay_minutes' — set exactly one.

delay_minutes.description: Fire this many minutes from now. Minimum 1. Mutually exclusive with 'at' — set exactly one.

initiation.description: Who wanted this message scheduled. Defaults to own_followup (your own check-in on in-flight work); pass human_request when a person asked you to remind them or to come back at a set time.

message.description: The text to deliver. Write it assuming your current conversation context — this session continues, it does not start fresh.

name.description: Short human-readable label for this reminder as it appears in the user's list of scheduled tasks (e.g. "Re-check PR #123 CI"). A few words, one line. Optional — omit and one is derived from the message.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__send_message
tools.description: Send a message to another Claude Code Remote session. It arrives there as a turn marked as sent by this session, not typed by a person: the target is told to treat it as data from a peer, and not to change permission settings or take new destructive actions on it alone. The call returns when the message is delivered, not when it is answered; the target can reply with its own send_message, which arrives here as a new turn. Use this for meta-orchestration — e.g. asking a sibling session to perform a subtask. A Claude Tag session (the Claude that answers in a Slack channel, thread or DM) cannot reply this way, even in a thread your user started: what it posts in answer goes to that conversation, not here.

schema.description: Send a message to another Claude Code Remote session. A Claude Tag session (the Claude that answers in a Slack channel, thread or DM) cannot reply this way, even in a thread your user started: what it posts in answer goes to that conversation, not here.

attachments.description: Optional. PROJECT CHANNEL SESSIONS only (a project's ambient session): uploads this session received that the target thread should read — each file_uuid is the file's id as your turn's uploads listing shows it (file_..., or a bare UUID) and must be on a person's message in this project. Refused from any other session or target.

in_reply_to.description: STANDING sessions only, for visibility 'posted_to_shared_channel'. The ts of the message from your principal that this answers: copy it from that message's <standing_owner_message ts="..."> envelope attribute (e.g. "1700000000.000200"). The server verifies it is one of your principal's own messages, then threads your reply under it. Omit it only when the message answers no specific message from your principal; the reply then threads under your principal's latest message. Invalid from any other session.

message.description: The message text. Bounded to 64 KiB.

priority.description: Optional queue-scheduling hint for the target session's event loop. One of: now, next, later. 'now' interrupts the current turn; 'next' joins the running turn without stopping it; 'later' waits for turn end. When omitted, the target session applies its default scheduling.

session_id.description: The target session ID to send a message to. Required unless a STANDING session addresses by role via to — leave it empty then.

slack_message_ts.description: SLACK CHANNEL SESSIONS only, when messaging a thread session in your channel: the id of a person's <message> to hand over as their own words, ahead of your note. The server verifies it and delivers it verbatim, or fails with a reason. Send it only to a thread whose pending proposal it clearly answers, or to each thread the person named or their ask covers. A bare "go" typed in one thread goes to that thread only.

thread_ts.description: With to "thread": the Slack ts of the thread's root message (like "1700000000.000200").

to.description: STANDING sessions only: address the destination by role instead of session_id. "parent" is your channel session (the same destination as session_id "@parent"). "thread" is the dedicated session of a thread in your channel; pass thread_ts with it (your spawn context names your origin thread's ts when you have one). To answer your principal in a thread they asked in, combine to "thread" with visibility "posted_to_shared_channel" and in_reply_to. When a route would work, a refusal names it (usually to "parent"). Leave session_id empty when using to. The tool result states where the message was actually delivered. Invalid from any other session.

visibility.description: STANDING sessions only: where this message ends up. Invalid from any other session.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__subscribe_pr_activity
tools.description: Subscribe this session to GitHub activity on a pull request. Once subscribed, comments, reviews, CI results and other PR events are delivered into this conversation as <wake reason="external-event"><event source="github" ...> envelopes. This tool call is idempotent. Use this when asked to autofix, monitor, watch, or babysit a PR. A PR's events go to one session at a time. If the tool result says a Claude agent is already watching the PR, the call succeeded but this session will not receive events: another conversation's Claude session, or a Claude agent that labels the PRs it watches, holds them. This session can take over only once that one stops: it unsubscribes or ends, or its watching label is removed from the PR.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__switch_environment
tools.description: Move THIS session onto another existing cloud environment the user can already use, without replacing this machine. Only the session's network changes: requests through the session's HTTPS proxy follow the target environment's allowed hosts, normally within seconds. Files, running processes and this conversation stay as they are. The target's variables are NOT set now: they are set from the next restart of Claude on this machine. Its setup script does NOT run now or at a restart: it runs only if the machine is replaced. Calling this tool IS the request for permission: the user is shown an approval prompt with the target's name and network, and must approve in every permission mode. So do not ask the user in chat first. Use it to move to an environment that get_environment lists in `saved_for_session_repositories`, or when the user asked to move this session. First call get_environment with the target's environment_id, then copy its `switch_statement` unchanged into `switch_statement`: the call is refused, changing nothing, if it does not match the target as it is when the user approves. Environments with unrestricted network access or a wildcard host are refused: start a new session on those instead. Network secrets saved on the target are sent to their hosts once this session has moved, and those saved on the current environment stop being used, which can take up to an hour; the approval prompt lists the hosts of both. If the user declines, or the call is refused, do not ask again in chat; carry on in this environment and say what remains blocked.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__update_environment
tools.description: Propose an edit to the cloud environment THIS session runs in. Calling this tool IS the request for permission: the user is shown an approval prompt with the exact change and who it affects, every time, in every permission mode, and nothing is changed unless they approve. The server separately checks that they may edit this environment (their own personal environment, or an organization environment if their role permits). So do NOT ask the user in chat first, and do not describe the change and wait for a reply: call get_environment, then say in one short sentence in your message what you are about to change and why, with the evidence, then call this tool. The approval prompt does not show your `reason`, so that sentence is the explanation they get. Use this tool when the task is blocked by the environment itself: a concrete need for network access, as get_environment's description defines it, or a missing non-secret environment variable. applies_to.description: The exact `applies_to` returned by get_environment: whose future sessions this edit changes. Shown to the person approving; the call is rejected if it does not match the environment.
enum: my personal environment: all of my future sessions that use it, not only this one

cron_expression.description: New 5-field cron expression. Fields without a prefix are UTC. By default, move the time 1 to 29 minutes earlier (for '9am', 8:31 to 8:59); use the number of letters in the task's name, modulo 29, plus 1. Runs that start between 6 AM and 9 AM Pacific time, which is 9 AM to noon Eastern time, can be delayed. If the user named no time, choose one outside those hours. ## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

Given in the session `session_2026-11-16-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMfdrQNV9XzGP4dyZm), in one typed message after pull request 238 registered the three questions (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/PROPAGATION-AND-CONSOLIDATION-ADJUDICATION.md`; the register in `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`). **Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "od68 different but how could this happen in first place"
>
> "od69 like the overall class of a parameter eg circulation for all the ones that deal with ramps and stairs and corridors and doors etc. the project is supposed to be like that"
>
> "od70 yes"

**Readings.**

- [ASSUMPTION: OD-68. "different" selects "two independent names": the same written word attested for one concept in one language and for another in a second language is two names, not a clash — basis: the word, against the three options the register gave]. The second clause is a question to the recorder, not a ruling, and is not recorded as one. It was answered in the session: it happens because a form is attested in its own language and a word in one language can mean another thing in a second (a homograph), and because a model-generated alias can attach a form to the wrong concept; the live database already holds forms under two concepts (`select lower(alias), count(distinct term_id) from term_aliases group by 1 having count(distinct term_id) > 1`).
- [ASSUMPTION: OD-69, part (a). "category" in the owner's question of 2026-11-16 means a concept's topic area, the overall class of a parameter: "circulation" for the parameters about ramps, stairs, corridors and doors, with the project organised by such classes — basis: the words and the example; it is the register's option (a), and `terms.domain` already carries `circulation`]. [GAP: whether the classes are a fixed list, who confirms the list, and which of the domains now in use are topic areas and which are kinds of concept that a parameter may not be (`functional_axis`, `methodology`, `medical`, `legal`, `economics`, `population` are the ones `dbcore.NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS` refuses) are NOT answered; the owner's words name the class and say the project "is supposed to be like that", and say nothing of a list. They are not read in.]
- [ASSUMPTION: OD-70. 130	```sql
131	-- sketch: one view, the only reader of "what is this concept called"
132	CREATE VIEW v_term_names AS
133	WITH attested AS (                  -- member forms a source uses; seeds are never vocabulary (E4)
134	    SELECT form_id, term_id, alias, upper(language) AS language, jurisdiction, attestation
135	      FROM term_aliases
136	     WHERE alias_type NOT IN ('NARROWER','BROADER')
137	       AND attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')),
138	en_instrument AS (                  -- English forms an instrument of an owed English-language jurisdiction uses
139	    SELECT a.* FROM attested a
140	     WHERE a.attestation = 'instrument' AND a.language = 'EN'
141	       AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_research_scope r
142	                    WHERE upper(r.language) = 'EN' AND r.jurisdiction = a.jurisdiction)),
143	pick AS (
144	    SELECT t.term_id, t.canonical_en,
145	           (SELECT form_id FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id
146	              AND lower(e.alias) = lower(t.canonical_en) ORDER BY form_id LIMIT 1) AS en_label_form,
147	           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id) AS en_first_form,
148	           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM attested o WHERE o.term_id = t.term_id
149	              AND o.attestation = 'instrument') AS origin_form
150	      FROM terms t)
151	SELECT p.term_id,
152	       p.canonical_en AS label,
153	       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attested a WHERE a.term_id = p.term_id
154	                 AND lower(a.alias) = lower(p.canonical_en)) AS label_is_attested_form,
155	       CASE WHEN p.en_label_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_label'
156	            WHEN p.en_first_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_form'
157	            WHEN p.origin_form   IS NOT NULL THEN 'origin_instrument_form'
158	            ELSE 'label_ours' END AS display_basis,
159	       COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form) AS display_form_id,
160	       COALESCE((SELECT alias FROM term_aliases f
161	                  WHERE f.form_id = COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form)),
162	                p.canonical_en) AS display_name,
163	       COALESCE((SELECT upper(language) FROM term_aliases f
164	                  WHERE f.form_id = COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form)),
165	                'EN') AS display_language,
166	       p.origin_form AS origin_form_id
167	  FROM pick p;

## Second stack: what each task changed, what was not taken, and what later tasks must read

_Derive the state with `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD`; the line-by-line account of what the critics found and did not repair is `scratchpad/session_2026-11-16-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack/sweep-list.md`._

T-010's domain refusal is kept. The ten live parameters carry no kind until T-109.

The pointer flag is `--source-row-id` (the column is `source_row_key`): `key` is a secret word to the refusal recorder. The renderer must hash-check and show only `reviewed` rows (T-037, amended).

Every reader listed in its sweep filters `retired_at IS NULL`; a new reader of either table must.

- **Proposed from the owner's questions on consolidation and propagation**: T-129 to T-135 and OD-68 to OD-70, adjudicated in `PROPAGATION-AND-CONSOLIDATION-ADJUDICATION.md`.

## 1. The four questions, verbatim, and what the pipeline does today

### Q1. "how does this pipeline handle identifying new topics for research, conducting them in another language, verifying a source is reputable, adjudicating how much of the source is relevant across different topics, writing down everything relevant including new topics if they don't already exist, judging the parameters for their values as well as assigning their codes as well as assigning evidence tier as well as determining category, and then synthesizing everything within the topic so that it can form a specification/determination?"

| Step the owner names | What does it today (verified) | What is missing |
|---|---|---|
| New topics | Seven stages in `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` (`python3 -c "import yaml;print([s['id'] for s in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/pipeline-contract.yaml'))['stages']])"`); a concept enters as `db.py observe-term` (verbatim, unjudged), is settled by `adjudicate-term` (outcomes from the column's CHECK: `python3 -I -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import dbcore;print(dbcore.check_values(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True),'term_adjudications','outcome'))"`), then `add-term`, `add-parameter` or `decline-parameter`. The quantity kind and its warrant on `add-parameter` are T-020's, on the stacked branch, not on `main`. | Consolidation after minting (Q2). |
| Another language | A search carries language and jurisdiction; coverage per parameter and bucket member (`lang_jur_map`, `v_coverage_*`); no back-translation (R11). A typed home for translations is T-049's (stacked branch: `git show origin/ccr-cc893571-i4lug4 --stat -- scripts/migrations | grep -i translat`); the renderer's gate for reviewed translations is T-037, not built. | Cross-language concept identity (T-028, open). |
| Reputable source | No "reputable" flag: R10 re-retrieval and the logged retrieval manifest, the author fidelity check, the verification standing `add-source` now requires (T-007, merged), and the tier computed from evidence type and scope (`grep -n 'def derive_tier' schemas/tier_derivation.py`; `adjudication_integrity`, blocking). Type and scope are judged. | The reconciliation of "tier and evidence-type assignment" being "permanently manual" (DR-2026-08-19 §12.5) with a computed tier is unrecorded: OD-70. |
| Relevance across topics | R16: every admission read against the whole parameter list (`record-scan`, `source_scans`, `v_scan_ledger`); relevance is extraction rows per parameter, not a score. | Executing the owed readings (T-105, T-031). |
| Writing down everything, new topics included | `add-extraction`, `observe-term`, the scan ledger's statuses. | — |
| Values, codes, tier | `source_value_extractions`; lens codes on `extraction_lens_links` (three lenses since 2026-11-16: identity, ICF, access need), written by judgment, the maps only proposing (MAPPING-DESIGN; T-126, open); tier as above. | T-126, T-127, T-128 (OD-67). |
| "Determining category" | Not one field. Five candidates hold: evidence type (judged) and tier (computed); claim type (`claim_type`); a concept's topic domain (`terms.domain`); quantity kind (T-020); design scale (`specifications.design_scale`). **Found here:** `terms.domain` has no CHECK (`grep -n -F 'has no CHECK, so there is no vocabulary' scripts/db.py`), `amend-term` accepts a domain only if a live row already carries it, and the non-quantity domains are a typed list in code (`grep -n '^NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS' scripts/dbcore.py`). | Which the owner meant: OD-69. |
| Synthesis and determination | `convergence_assessment` (Opus-only); `specifications` keyed on parameter plus at least one lens column, computed by the engine (`grep -n '^RULE_VERSION' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`), never hand-assigned (owner, 2026-09-09 evening). No determination is live: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute('select count(*), sum(retired_at is null) from specifications').fetchone())"`. | T-059, T-068, T-124, T-110. |

### Q2. "is there an iterative loop with limited repetitions to ensure exit such that you can ensure that topics across languages and synonyms are properly consolidated and associated in base with those consolidations propagating forward throughout database so we don't end up with duplicates or near identical topics?"

**Today: no.** Verified: a write-time near-duplicate refusal (`grep -n -A30 'def _near_terms' scripts/db.py`: token-set subset or superset against every label and every alias whose `attestation` is not `model_seed`, in any language; refused unless `--distinct-from` with a rationale); exact clashes (`_name_holder`); adjudication NAMES-EXISTING; `merge-parameter`, `rename-term`, `retire-parameter`. **There is no verb that merges two terms** (`python3 scripts/db.py --help | tr ',{}' '\n\n\n' | grep -c -x -E 'merge-term|retire-term'` prints 0; G2 is confirmed, every parser read, not only the names). Bounded iteration exists only for citation mining (depth 1, `grep -n 'Depth-1 enforced' skills/citation-miner_SKILL.md`) and a recorded `saturation_signal` on `search_executions`.

**What the findings did not say, found here.** (a) Forms are already shared by two concepts in one language: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select upper(language), lower(alias), group_concat(distinct term_id), group_concat(distinct attestation) from term_aliases where alias_type not in ('NARROWER','BROADER') group by 1,2 having count(distinct term_id)>1\").fetchall())"`. Some are seeds; some are unrecorded aliases; at least one is a homonym (the Spanish "paso libre" is held by both the corridor-width and the door-width concepts), which a judge records as two concepts rather than merges. (b) `add-term --distinct-from` keeps the judgment that two near names are two concepts only inside the new term's adjudication `rationale` (`grep -n -B2 -A12 'near = \[(t, h) for t, h in _near_terms' scripts/db.py`), so no later pass can know the pair was judged. (c) T-029's file names "a merge (`merge-parameter`, `rename-term`)" as the act for two terms that name one concept (`grep -n -F 'the act is a merge' workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-029-term-relations.md`); neither verb merges terms. (d) `merge-parameter` re-points every row that holds the folded id (UPDATE) and records the move as a dated `MERGED` line appended to each moved row's `notes`, the shape the 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement forbids ("a correction appended to a note"); it has never been run (`python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select count(*) from base_parameters where status='merged'\").fetchone())"`).

### Q3. "you have identified missing items. what else exists in pipeline that allows us to work in all directions and systematically perform new passes over already-recorsed rows to ensure that the database codes/terms/etc are consistently applied as well as to append existing rows with more information as required if the base gets extended?"

**Today: owed passes are derived and listed; they are run by research batches; there is no scheduler and none is wanted.** Verified: `v_scan_ledger`, `v_reading_owed`, `v_deferred_acts` (T-079, merged: a deferral stands while its cell is owed, and follows `merged_into`), `scan_debt` (advisory, red whenever debt exists, no baseline by design), `verified_scan_integrity` (advisory, red on extractions with no recorded reading), the `v_coverage_*` views, `unmined`, `unmined-gaps`, `cell-status`, `coverage`, and the COVERAGE reads of `/batch-done` (T-090, merged; `grep -n '## COVERAGE' .claude/commands/batch-done.md`). Appending to a recorded figure is by new pointer rows (`add-lens-link`, `retire-lens-link`, `add-population-icf-link`, `retire-identity` with a successor), retire-in-place (specifications; admission edges and connections once T-050 merges) and narrow `amend-*` verbs. **One re-pass per kind of base extension**, which is the answer to the question:

| The base grows by | The rows that may now owe more | Derived by | Executed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| a parameter | every held source × the new parameter | `v_scan_ledger`, `scan_debt`; T-031's clause inventory and re-read flag | T-105 and every batch (R16) |
| a lens code or map row | figures recorded before the base could propose a group | T-126's audit lists (i) and, by this adjudication's amendment, (iii) | T-127, T-106 and their successors |
| a form, a seed or a translation | pairs of concepts that may be one | T-130's `consolidation-candidates` (new) | T-131 and every later batch, through `/batch-done` |
| a language-jurisdiction pair | concepts with no form there | T-057's base coverage view; `v_research_scope` | T-107 |
| a source's verification or tier, a grading, an edge | a stored determination | `derivation_handshake_integrity` (recompute) | retire and re-determine; blocking once T-132 lands |

### Q4. "in fact, how does the pipeline handle propagation in all directions whenever there is a change made to a row or a new row somewhere is made?"

**By pull and by refusal, not by push.** Verified: the schema holds one trigger (`python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='trigger'\").fetchall())"`); a change reaches dependents because they point at the row (the views: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select count(*) from sqlite_master where type='view'\").fetchone())"`; the findings' figure is the stacked branch's, which adds `v_translations_current`); through a cascade held in one place (`merge-parameter`, successor columns, `merged_into` followed by `v_deferred_acts`); through writers that refuse until dependents are handled (merge and retire refuse a live determination and an open gate); through determinations as recomputable caches (`derivation_sha` hashes the graded link set, each figure's in-lens state and the three lens codes; `derivation_handshake_integrity` recomputes the rest); through the capture path (scratch copy, `dbcore.writable_tables`, `emit_batch_sql.py`, migration only) and the replay checks; and through read-only audits. **Corrected here:** the findings (G7) name "the verification cron" as a route that bypasses the writers; it was deleted on 2026-10-14 (`grep -n -F 'The scheduled cron that polled this pool was deleted' scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py`). Three sentences still name it as live (`grep -n -i cron scripts/audit/derivation_handshake_integrity.py scripts/assess/assess_cell.py governance/research-contract.yaml`): prose callers, repaired by T-132.

## 2. The adjudication, gap by gap

Order of preference for every fix (CLAUDE.md §8): do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then the smallest code. Tests in priority: (1) layer compliance, (2) long-term provenance, (3) long-term consistency, (4) minimal code.

| Gap | Decision | The fix, in one line | Why this and not another |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G1** no bounded consolidation sweep | **NEW: T-130 (tooling), T-131 (research)**, on T-129 | a read verb proposes candidate pairs for four derived reasons; an Opus judge merges, relates or keeps apart; stop when a pass proposes nothing or at `consolidation.max_passes` (3) in the contract | the candidates, the bound and the record of who judged are each held once (data, the contract, the judging rows); a stored candidate list or a pass counter would be a second home of derivable facts (rule 8); a check red while candidates exist would be red by construction (rule 6), so the list is printed by `/batch-done` |
| **G2** no `merge-term` | **NEW: T-129** (design `tasks/T-129-design.md` §A) | a merge is a `term_merges` row (judge, time, reason, retire-in-place), `v_term_survivor` derives each term's survivor, every writer refuses a folded term naming the survivor, every concept reader reads the survivor's class; `add-term --distinct-from` writes a T-029 `distinct` row | test 2: a re-point would overwrite adjudications and forms (the records of what was said); a row plus a derived survivor keeps them, as `retire-identity`, `specifications` and `translations` already do |

8485	    """Prove `entry_ref` names an entry in the catalogue file; return how it resolved.
8486

8488	    the file the CHECK names, dispatching on its format. A format with no resolver here
8489	    is refused: adding a catalogue is a schema change and an owner ruling, and its
8490	    resolver arrives with it.
8491	    """
8492	    path = dbcore.REPO_ROOT / catalogue
8493	    if not path.is_file():
8494	        raise Refusal(f"--catalogue {catalogue!r}: the file is not in this checkout.")
8495	    if path.suffix == ".md":
8496	        if entry_ref.startswith("["):
8497	            raise Refusal(f"--entry-ref {entry_ref!r}: a bracketed value is the registry's "
8498	                          f"template placeholder, not an entry.")
8499	        needle = f'standard_cited: "{entry_ref}"'
8500	        if needle not in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
8501	            raise Refusal(f"--entry-ref {entry_ref!r}: no registry entry in {catalogue} "
8502	                          f"reads {needle}. Give the entry's standard_cited value exactly.")
8503	        return f"{catalogue} {needle}"
8504	    if path.suffix == ".json":
8505	        entries = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
8506	        if not any(isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("ref_id") == entry_ref for e in entries):
8507	            raise Refusal(f"--entry-ref {entry_ref!r}: no entry in {catalogue} has that "

8544	    """Mint a term from a PERMITTED catalogue on the owner's recorded approval.
8545	
8546	    THE OWNER'S D3 ANSWER, 2026-10-09. "D3 keep the rule" (names that come out of
8547	    research come from observed phrases, add-term --from-observation), then "D3 for
8548	    parameter terms? it can be pulled from previous catalogues of entries for
8549	    prepopulating", and, from listed options, the catalogues "Code and standards
8550	    registries" and "Old corpus terms" (NOT the old Part 4 item names) and the guard
8551	    "Screen, then you approve". insert_term refuses to mint without an observation, so
8552	    this is the second route, and it is narrow by construction:
8553	
8554	      SCREEN: canonical_en with no digit, comparator or min/max word (_VALUE_BEARING, the
8555	      add-term guard) and no [A-Z]-NN item code; a definition with no value either; not a
8556	      name or alias any term already holds; and an entry_ref that resolves inside the
8557	      catalogue file (_resolve_catalogue_entry).

8559	      `## ` heading, occurring EXACTLY ONCE in references/project-standards.md. That proves
8560	      the entry exists and is unambiguous. It does NOT prove the entry approves this name,
8561	      or that the name appears in the entry_ref: neither is compared, and the owner's
8562	      "Screen, then you approve" step (ledger 2026-10-09) is a process step no code checks.
8563	
8564	    The catalogue, the entry and the approval pointer are written on the term row itself
8565	    (terms.catalogue, catalogue_entry_ref, catalogue_approval_ref; RULINGS R25). No

8602	                              f"item subject {subject!r}. A name taken from a catalogue is "
8603	                              f"the catalogue's own words, never a model's rewording (OR-17).")

8607	                          f"{clash['term_id']}. Nothing was written.")
8608	        if clash:
8609	            raise Refusal(f"mint-term-from-catalogue: {canonical_en!r} is an alias "
8610	                          f"({clash['detail']}) of {clash['term_id']}: the concept is held. "
8611	                          f"Nothing was written.")

8613	        row = {"term_id": term_id, "canonical_en": canonical_en, "definition": definition,
8614	               "domain": (domain or "").strip() or None,
8615	               "scope_note": (scope_note or "").strip() or None,
8616	               "catalogue": catalogue, "catalogue_entry_ref": entry_ref,
8617	               "catalogue_approval_ref": approval_ref}
8618	        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "terms", session))

    """Append one row to search_executions. Returns its exec_id.

    `form_ids` are rowids of term_aliases rows, read now (T-026): the forms this search
    fired. One search_execution_forms row per distinct form is written with that form's KEY
    (term_id, alias, language), never the rowid, which the capture path does not carry.
    `terms_used` is refused for a new row (the JSON held term ids and free words, so no word
    maps mechanically to a form); the column stays for the rows that already carry it.

    A search names what it looked for: a `slug`, a `parameter_id` (a catalogue
    search for one design parameter, R43) or a `mined_ref_id` (a pass over one
    source). Any one will do; none is refused.

            for col in ("parameter_id", *_LENS_COLUMNS, "jurisdiction", "language"):
                if row[col] is not None and sub[col] is not None and row[col] != sub[col]:
                    raise Refusal(f"--gap-id {gap_id} is a gap in {col} {sub[col]!r} (subject from "
                                  f"{sub['subject_home']}), but this search is for {col} {row[col]!r}. A search "
                                  f"names the gap it was run to close; fix the flag or the gap. Nothing was written.")
        # The forms this search fired, resolved BEFORE the execution row is written: a rowid
        # is input only, and what is stored is the form's key.
        forms = {}
        for fid in form_ids or []:
            frow = conn.execute("SELECT term_id, alias, language FROM term_aliases "
                                "WHERE rowid = ?", [fid]).fetchone()
            if frow is None:
                raise Refusal(f"--form-id {fid} names no term_aliases row. Read the rowid now "
                              f"(select rowid, term_id, alias, language from term_aliases). "
                              f"Nothing was written.")
            if frow["language"].upper() != language:
                raise Refusal(f"--form-id {fid} is the {frow['language']!r} form "
                              f"{frow['alias']!r}, but this search is --language {language!r}: a "
                              f"search fires the forms of its own language. Nothing was written.")
            forms[tuple(frow)] = None
        if mined_ref_id and not conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?", [mined_ref_id]).fetchone():
            # Named, not a bare FOREIGN KEY constraint failed -- same discipline as
            # the --admitted-ref-id check below.
            raise Refusal(
                f"--mined-ref-id {mined_ref_id} is not in evidence_sources. File "
                f"the source first, then log the pass that mined it.")
        # DERIVED, NEVER HAND-TYPED. This table's audit columns were spelled
        # `session` and `executed_at` here as string literals until migration
        # 085 renamed them to the corpus-wide `created_by_session`/`created_at`.
        # That rename's sweep was empirical -- it ran the check battery against
        # a rebuilt DB -- and it could not see these two, because NO CHECK
        # WRITES A SEARCH EXECUTION. The battery stayed green and `log-search`,
        # the first command of every research batch, raised "table
        # search_executions has no column named session" on its next call.
        # Every writer that reached for stamp_for instead survived the same
        # rename untouched, which is the whole argument for deriving: the
        # schema is the one home of the column's name (rule 8).
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "search_executions", session))
        # Keep the junction rows stamped with the execution row's own instant
        # rather than a second, slightly later `now()`.
        ts = row.get("created_at", ts)
        cols = ", ".join(row)
        ph = ", ".join(["?"] * len(row))
        cur = conn.execute(
            f"INSERT INTO search_executions ({cols}) VALUES ({ph})",
            list(row.values()))
        exec_id = cur.lastrowid
        # ONE carrier: search_admissions. Until 2026-08-24 this dual-wrote the
        # same fact into admitted_ref_ids (JSON on the row) and kept the two
        # honest with parity checks H03/H04. Owner ruling 2026-08-24: "it is
        # better to have a table cell point to another table cell than to
        # rewrite" — a fact written into two tables is drift waiting to happen,
        # and a parity check does not prevent that, it makes it survivable and
        # therefore permanent. Nothing ever READ the JSON: it was write-only
        # data guarded by a test. The junction is the record, and it carries its
        # own created_at.
        for ref_id in ids:
            if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?",
                                [ref_id]).fetchone():
                # Named, not a bare FOREIGN KEY constraint failed. The whole
                # transaction rolls back, execution row included.
                raise Refusal(
                    f"--admitted-ref-id {ref_id} is not in evidence_sources. "
                    f"File the source first (`db.py add-source`), then log the "
                    f"search that admitted it.")
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO search_admissions "
                "(exec_id, ref_id, created_at, created_by_session) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", [exec_id, ref_id, ts, session])
        for term_id, alias, flang in forms:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO search_execution_forms "
                "(exec_id, term_id, alias, language, created_at, created_by_session) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", [exec_id, term_id, alias, flang, ts, session])
        _link_result_artefacts(conn, exec_id, result_artefacts,
                               mined_ref_id=mined_ref_id, query_text=query_text,
                               session=session, ts=ts)
        return exec_id

CREATE TABLE term_aliases (
    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    alias               TEXT NOT NULL,
    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
    alias_type          TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK(alias_type IN (
                            'SYNONYM','TRANSLATION','NARROWER',
                            'BROADER','DEPRECATED','DOMAIN'
                        )),
    jurisdiction        TEXT,
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL, observation_id INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id), attestation TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unrecorded'
    CHECK (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source','owner_supplied','model_seed','unrecorded')), source_url TEXT
    CHECK (source_url IS NULL OR (
        (source_url GLOB 'http://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*'

def request_translation(source_table, source_column, source_row_key, target_language, stage, due_stage=None, *,
                        session, dry_run=False, contract_path=None):
    """Ask for a translation of one cell. The cell is read here and only its hash is stored: no argument carries
    the original. Refused: a pointer that does not resolve (no such table or column, a table with no single-column
    primary key, no such row, a cell that is not text or is empty), a target language lang_jur_map does not hold or
    that is the pointed row's own language, a stage that is not a stage id of the contract, and a cell that already
    has a current translation into that language (the refusal names `--supersedes`)."""
    _require_translation_session(session, "request-translation")
    contract = _translation_contract(contract_path)
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        tid, created = _open_translation_request(conn, source_table, source_column, source_row_key, target_language,
                                                 stage, due_stage, contract, session, "request-translation")
    return {"translation_id": tid, "created": created, "status": "requested", "dry_run": dry_run}


def record_translation(text, translator_kind, translator_name, *, translation_id=None, source_table=None,
                       source_column=None, source_row_key=None, target_language=None, stage=None, due_stage=None,
                       supersedes=None, session, dry_run=False, contract_path=None):
    """Answer a request by id, or open and answer one in one call by pointer (exactly one of the two forms).

    Refused: both forms or neither; a translation that adds, drops or changes a number of the original
    (`translation_number_gaps`); a cell whose hash no longer matches the request's (request it again); a request
    that is not `requested`. `--supersedes M` retires translation M in place, in the same transaction; it is refused
    unless M is translated or reviewed, not already retired, and translates the same pointer into the same language.
    The original is never touched."""
    ctx = "record-translation"
    _require_translation_session(session, ctx)
    pointer = (source_table, source_column, source_row_key, target_language, stage)
    if translation_id is not None and any(p is not None for p in pointer + (due_stage,)):
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: pass --translation-id OR the pointer (--source-table, --source-column, "
                      f"--source-row-id, --target-language, --stage), never both. Nothing was written.")
    if translation_id is None and not all((p or "").strip() for p in pointer):
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: pass --translation-id, or the whole pointer: --source-table, --source-column, "
                      f"--source-row-id, --target-language and --stage. Nothing was written.")
    text, name = (text or "").strip(), (translator_name or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --text is blank. Nothing was written.")
    if not name:
        raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --translator-name is required: the model id, the tool and version, or the person. "
                      f"Nothing was written.")
    contract = _translation_contract(contract_path)
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "translations", "translator_kind", translator_kind, ctx)
        old = None
        if supersedes is not None:
            old = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM translations WHERE translation_id=?", (supersedes,)).fetchone()
            if not old or old["status"] not in ("translated", "reviewed") or old["superseded_by_translation_id"]:
                raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: --supersedes {supersedes} is not a current translation (translated or "
                              f"reviewed, and not already retired). Nothing was written.")
        if translation_id is None:
            tid, _ = _open_translation_request(conn, source_table, source_column, source_row_key, target_language,
                                               stage, due_stage, contract, session, ctx, replacing=supersedes)
        else:
            tid = translation_id
        req = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM translations WHERE translation_id=?", (tid,)).fetchone()
        if not req:
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: no translation request {tid}. Nothing was written.")
        if req["status"] != "requested":
            raise Refusal(f"{ctx}: translation {tid} is {req['status']}, not requested. A corrected translation "
                          f"is a new row: record it against the pointer with --supersedes {tid}. "

173	def make_pdf(pages):
174	    """A minimal valid PDF, one Helvetica text line per page -- no PDF library needed,
175	    so the case that reads it runs wherever the checks run."""
176	    def esc(t):
177	        return t.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("(", "\\(").replace(")", "\\)")
178	    objs = {1: "<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
179	            3: "<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>"}
180	    kids, nid = [], 4
181	    for text in pages:
182	        stream = f"BT /F1 12 Tf 72 720 Td ({esc(text)}) Tj ET"
183	        objs[nid + 1] = f"<< /Length {len(stream)} >>\nstream\n{stream}\nendstream"
184	        objs[nid] = (f"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 612 792] /Contents "
185	                     f"{nid + 1} 0 R /Resources << /Font << /F1 3 0 R >> >> >>")
186	        kids.append(f"{nid} 0 R")
187	        nid += 2
188	    objs[2] = f"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [{' '.join(kids)}] /Count {len(pages)} >>"
189	    out, offs = b"%PDF-1.4\n", {}
190	    for i in sorted(objs):
191	        offs[i] = len(out)
192	        out += f"{i} 0 obj\n{objs[i]}\nendobj\n".encode("latin-1")
193	    xref = len(out)
194	    out += f"xref\n0 {len(objs) + 1}\n0000000000 65535 f \n".encode()
195	    for i in sorted(objs):
196	        out += f"{offs[i]:010d} 00000 n \n".encode()
197	    out += (f"trailer\n<< /Size {len(objs) + 1} /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n{xref}\n"
198	            f"%%EOF\n").encode()
199	    return out

print("Section A7: equivalence before minting; NAMES-NEW only through add-term")
near = q("SELECT t.term_id, t.canonical_en FROM terms t JOIN base_parameters p USING (term_id) "
         "WHERE t.canonical_en LIKE '% %' ORDER BY length(t.canonical_en) DESC LIMIT 1")
obs = scalar("SELECT observation_id FROM observed_terms WHERE context_quote IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1")
if not near or obs is None:
    for t_ in ("T01", "T02", "T03"):
        skip(t_, "no parameter term of two words, or no observation with a quote")
else:
    near = near[0]
    words = near["canonical_en"].split()
    subset_name = " ".join(words[:-1]) + "s"          # token subset, plural: 'ramp runs' shape
    # add-term now requires the name to lie inside the observed phrase (owner E1, 2026-11-06), so
    # the probe observes the phrase it then tries to mint.
    obs = db.observe_term({"ref_id": scalar("SELECT ref_id FROM observed_terms WHERE observation_id=?", obs),
                           "surface_form": subset_name, "language": "EN", "locator": "fixture",
                           "context_quote": f"a fixture sentence using {subset_name} once",
                           "verbatim_exempt": "fixture text: no retrieval artefact carries it"}, S)["observation_id"]
    r = refusal(db.insert_term, obs, subset_name, "probe", session=S, dry_run=True)
    record("T01", f"add-term refuses {subset_name!r} beside {near['term_id']} {near['canonical_en']!r}",
           r and near["term_id"] in r, r)
    res, err = ok(db.insert_term, obs, subset_name, "probe", session=S, dry_run=True,
                  distinct_from=[near["term_id"]])
    record("T02", "accepted when --distinct-from names the near term", res is not None, err)
    r = refusal(db.adjudicate_term, obs, "NAMES-NEW", "probe", session=S, term_id=near["term_id"],
                dry_run=True)
    record("T03", "adjudicate-term refuses NAMES-NEW, naming add-term", r and "add-term" in r, r)

print("Section A11: a harm finding carries its insufficient edge")
r = refusal(db.insert_extraction, extraction(FULL_REF, P_FULL, figure_role="finding",
                                             harm_finding=1),

    # ── D: decline-parameter, and add-parameter's refusal of a declined term ─────
    # Migration 101. Fixture terms are minted through the writers (observe-term ->
    # add-term) on the copy, never a live id; names carry no digit, comparator or min/max
    # word, because add-term refuses a value-bearing name.
    decline = getattr(db, "decline_parameter", None)
    if decline is None:
        # The pre-101 state: no verb and no table. Recorded rather than raised, so the
        # run still prints its summary and exits 1.
        record("D00", "db.decline_parameter exists (migration 101's writer)", False,
               "no such function -- parameter_declinations has no writer")
    else:
        # A sighting since migration 102: a new observation carries a locator and a quote
        # containing the phrase, and a fixture quote no artefact holds takes the recorded
        # exemption route (observe-term --verbatim-exempt), as a real one would.
        def sighting(ref, phrase):
            return {"ref_id": ref, "surface_form": phrase, "language": "EN",
                    "locator": "fixture locator",
                    "context_quote": f"a fixture sentence using {phrase} once",
                    "verbatim_exempt": "fixture text: no retrieval artefact carries it"}

        # The exemption is refused where a decodable body is held (observe-term shares
        # add-extraction's refusal, R2-6), and the first source by id holds one, so the
        # sighting is made on the first source that holds none (derived, never named).
        BODYLESS = next(r for (r,) in q("SELECT ref_id FROM evidence_sources WHERE "
                                        "superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL ORDER BY ref_id")
                        if not db._retrieval_log().decodable_body_artefacts(r))

        def fixture_term(name):
            obs = db.observe_term(sighting(BODYLESS, f"fixture phrase: {name}"), S)
            return db.insert_term(obs["observation_id"], name, "fixture rationale",
                                  S)["term_id"]

        def declinations(term_id):
            return q("SELECT reason, created_by_session FROM parameter_declinations "
                     "WHERE term_id=?", term_id)

-- 145_retire_admissions_and_connections_in_place.sql
-- SCHEMA migration (T-050; OD-29, resolved under delegation: a connection and a search-to-source admission edge are
-- data rows under the owner's ruling of 2026-09-16, "RETIRE IN PLACE, NEVER HARD-DELETE"; a genuine deletion of either
-- is an exception only the owner rules on). No data rows.
--
-- `search_admissions` and `connections` each gain the retirement shape `specifications` and `extraction_lens_links`
-- already use: `retired_at`, `retired_by_session` and `retirement_reason`, nullable, set together or not at all. The
-- CHECK sits on the last of the three, because SQLite adds a column by ALTER and a column constraint may name its
-- siblings. `connection_targets` gains nothing: a target of a retired connection is retired through its pointer.
--
-- THE RULING'S EXECUTION CONDITION: "No row is retired in place until every reader that could surface it filters on
-- status." The two views that read `search_admissions` filter below; every other reader of either table is a script and
-- is fixed in the same pull request (db.py, research_batch_dod.py, test_db_integrity.py, graph/extract_db.py).
--  * v_source_admission, from its current text in sqlite_master (migration 070 set it), gains `AND sa.retired_at IS NULL`:
--    a withdrawn attribution is not "the search that admitted this source".
--  * v_coverage_parameter_via_admission, from its current text (migration 140 set it), gains the same predicate in the
--    `reached` CTE: a search does not reach a parameter through an admission it has withdrawn. No view reads
--    `connections` or `connection_targets`.
-- The retired edge stays a row: it is the record that the claim was made, when, by whom and why it was withdrawn, and it
-- is never un-retired in place (db.py link-admission refuses it and names log-search).
-- WRITERS: db.py unlink-admission and delete-connection (each now sets the three columns instead of deleting).
-- READERS: the two views above, db.py get_connections, db.py's parameter reach, research_batch_dod R17,
-- test_db_integrity S01 and the graph extractor.

ALTER TABLE search_admissions ADD COLUMN retired_at TEXT;
ALTER TABLE search_admissions ADD COLUMN retired_by_session TEXT;
ALTER TABLE search_admissions ADD COLUMN retirement_reason TEXT
  CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL) AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL));

ALTER TABLE connections ADD COLUMN retired_at TEXT;
ALTER TABLE connections ADD COLUMN retired_by_session TEXT;
ALTER TABLE connections ADD COLUMN retirement_reason TEXT
  CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL) AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL));

DROP VIEW v_source_admission;
CREATE VIEW v_source_admission AS
SELECT
    es.ref_id,
    es.pub_title,
    es.tier                     AS source_tier,

-- SCHEMA migration -- a concept is its id; its names are forms, one row per occurrence; `canonical_en` is our label.
-- Tooling (IMP-21, workplan T-028; design workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-028-design.md, revised

-- judge picks; the pick is recorded with its reason"). No research rows.
--
-- AFTER_DATA: 20261106053823
-- (Why the marker: `migrate_db.py --rebuild` runs schema migrations before the data migrations that follow the last

-- after this reshape and the rebuild would diverge. Value: the newest data migration at the time of writing, derived by
-- `ls scripts/migrations/data_*.sql | sed -E 's/.*data_([0-9]{14})_.*/\1/' | sort | tail -1`.)
--
-- WHAT CHANGES (design sections 3, 7 and 10):
--  1. term_aliases is rebuilt to ONE ROW PER OCCURRENCE: a surrogate key `form_id` (assigned here, once, from each row's
--     rowid; the rebuild reproduces it and nothing stored points by rowid), a unique occurrence index in place of the
--     primary key (term_id, alias, language), and a nullable `usage_type` (NULL = not yet typed, the truth for every
--     existing row; typed by judgment when the row is next touched, never guessed here). The column definitions T-026
--     added are copied from sqlite_master, so `attestation` keeps its DEFAULT 'unrecorded'. Legacy alias_type values
--     are not rewritten.
--  2. T-026's junction search_execution_forms is remapped BY KEY to form_id before the old table is dropped: at the
--     occurrence grain the old key is no longer unique, and a foreign key on it would answer `foreign key mismatch`.
--     Until now one row per key, so the join is exact and the junction's row count does not change.
--  3. term_label_picks: the one home of the judge, the reason and the former label of a label set by judgment (OD-38).
--     The route is derived from which pointer is set; the new label is terms.canonical_en, never copied here.
--  4. v_term_names: the name shown (E1) and whether our label is also an attested form, derived; no label-kind column
--     and no display pointer is stored.
-- No VACUUM: it may renumber the implicit rowids of every table without an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY.

CREATE TABLE _146_term_aliases (
    form_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    alias               TEXT NOT NULL,
    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
    alias_type          TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK(alias_type IN (
                            'SYNONYM','TRANSLATION','NARROWER',
                            'BROADER','DEPRECATED','DOMAIN'
                        )),
    jurisdiction        TEXT,
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    attestation         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unrecorded'
    CHECK (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source','owner_supplied','model_seed','unrecorded')),
    source_url          TEXT
    CHECK (source_url IS NULL OR (
        (source_url GLOB 'http://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*'
         OR source_url GLOB 'https://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')
        AND source_url NOT GLOB '*[' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')),
    source_page         TEXT
    CHECK (source_page IS NULL OR TRIM(source_page, char(32,9,10,13)) <> ''),
    source_line         INTEGER
    CHECK (source_line IS NULL OR (typeof(source_line) = 'integer' AND source_line > 0)),
    source_clause       TEXT
    CHECK (
        (source_clause IS NULL OR TRIM(source_clause, char(32,9,10,13)) <> '') AND
        -- an attested occurrence says where
        (attestation NOT IN ('instrument','other_source')
         OR observation_id IS NOT NULL
         OR (source_url IS NOT NULL AND (source_page IS NOT NULL OR source_clause IS NOT NULL)))
        -- a seed or an unrecorded form says nowhere
        AND (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')
         OR (source_url IS NULL AND source_page IS NULL AND source_line IS NULL
             AND source_clause IS NULL))
    ),
    -- the sixth statement of 2026-11-06's usage types, in this column's own CHECK (read by dbcore.check_values)

    CHECK (usage_type IS NULL OR usage_type IN

);

                               source_url, source_page, source_line, source_clause, usage_type)
SELECT rowid, term_id, alias, language, alias_type, jurisdiction, notes, created_at,
       created_by_session, updated_at, updated_by_session, observation_id, attestation,
       source_url, source_page, source_line, source_clause, NULL
  FROM term_aliases;

CREATE TABLE _146_search_execution_forms (
    exec_id            INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES search_executions(exec_id),

);

  FROM search_execution_forms j JOIN _146_term_aliases a USING (term_id, alias, language);
