def rename_term(term_id: str, canonical_en: str, reason: str, session: str,
                from_observation: int = None, ruling_quote: str = None,
                dry_run: bool = False, *, from_form: int = None, judge: str = None):
    """Correct a term's label, recording who picked it, why, and what it replaced.

    `amend-term` refused canonical_en since 2026-09-25 ("a vocabulary decision with
    callers, not a wording fix"), and no other verb could change it, so an answer-shaped
    or mis-chosen name was permanent (critique F5; plan section 1.2 item 6: the held ADA
    text says "turning space" and not "turning circle"). This is that vocabulary
    decision, with its warrant required, exactly one of:

      --from-form F         an ATTESTED member form of THIS term (instrument or other_source,
                            not NARROWER or BROADER) whose text is the new label: the stored
                            pick of the name shown when several English instruments name the
                            concept differently (T-028; OD-38, owner 2026-11-12: "First recorded,
                            until a named judge picks; the pick is recorded with its reason");
      --from-observation N  the new name comes from a phrase a source USES, in the
                            source's own language (owner E1, 2026-11-06: a concept first
                            met outside English is named by that phrase), whose latest adjudication names
                            THIS term, whose surface form
                            contains the new name (the 2026-09-09 rule, kept by the owner
                            on 2026-10-09: names come from observed phrases);
      --ruling-quote "..."  or from the owner's own words, quoted verbatim and found
                            exactly once in references/project-standards.md, containing
                            the new name.
    Every route names its --judge (who picked) beside the --reason (OD-38).

    Nothing else moves: parameters, adjudications and extractions point at term_id, so the
    name is reached, never copied (rule 5). The label is not a form (OD-03), so the former
    label is NOT written into term_aliases and no AMENDED trailer is appended to scope_note
    (the owner's schema-shape statement of 2026-11-06: a correction appended to a note is a fact
    in the wrong cell): one term_label_picks row holds the former label, the route's one pointer,
    the judge and the reason. No other term may hold the new name, as a label or as an attested
    English form (_name_holder); a seed never refuses (E4).

    REFUSES: no judge; neither or several warrants; a value-bearing name (_VALUE_BEARING, as
    add-term); a quote not exactly once in the ledger or not containing the name; an observation
    whose latest adjudication does not name this term, or that does not contain the name; a form
    that is not an attested member form of this term or whose text is not the name; a name another
    term holds.
    """
    new = (canonical_en or "").strip()
    if not new:
        raise Refusal("rename-term: --canonical-en is required: a term is its name.")
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(reason, term_id)
    judge = (judge or "").strip()
    if not judge:
        raise Refusal("rename-term: --judge is required: who picked this label (OD-38, owner 2026-11-12: "
                      "the pick is recorded with its reason, and a pick names its judge). Nothing was written.")
    if (from_observation is not None) + bool((ruling_quote or "").strip()) + (from_form is not None) != 1:
        raise Refusal(
            "rename-term: give exactly one warrant for the new name -- --from-form F (an attested "
            "form of this term), --from-observation N (a phrase an admitted source uses) or "
            "--ruling-quote '<the owner's words>' (found once in references/project-standards.md). "
            "A name with no warrant is a name typed by hand, which the 2026-09-09 rule forbids.")
    vb = _VALUE_BEARING_NAME.search(new)
    if vb:
        raise Refusal(
            f"rename-term: {new!r} carries a number, a comparator or a min/max word "
            f"({vb.group(0)!r}), so it "
            f"states a determination in its own name -- the item-layer defect "
            f"(DR-2026-08-19 section 1.1). Name the quantity, never its value.")
    if ruling_quote:
        dbcore.require_ledger_quote_once(ruling_quote, "rename-term: the --ruling-quote",
                                         "That ties this rename to one ruling.")
        if new.lower() not in dbcore.normalise_quote_text(ruling_quote).lower():
            raise Refusal(f"rename-term: the quoted ruling does not contain {new!r}; the "
                          f"words that authorise a name must say it.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        term = conn.execute("SELECT term_id, canonical_en FROM terms "
                            "WHERE term_id = ?", (term_id,)).fetchone()
        if term is None:
            raise Refusal(f"rename-term: {term_id!r}: no such term.")
        old = term["canonical_en"]
        if old == new:
            return {"term_id": term_id, "changed": False, "dry_run": dry_run}
        for clash in _name_holder(conn, new, "EN", exclude_term=term_id)["clashes"]:
            if clash["kind"] == "label":
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: {new!r} is already the name of {clash['term_id']}. "
                              f"Two terms with one name are one concept twice; that is a merge, "
                              f"not a rename. Nothing was written.")
            raise Refusal(f"rename-term: {new!r} is an alias ({clash['detail']}, form {clash['form_id']}) of "
                          f"{clash['term_id']}, attested. A name another term answers to would make "
                          f"one phrase point at two concepts. Nothing was written.")
        if from_form is not None:
            form = conn.execute("SELECT form_id, alias, alias_type, attestation FROM term_aliases "
                                "WHERE form_id = ? AND term_id = ?", (from_form, term_id)).fetchone()
            if (form is None or form["attestation"] not in dbcore.ATTESTED_FORMS
                    or form["alias_type"] in ("NARROWER", "BROADER")):
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: form {from_form} is not an attested member form of {term_id} "
                              f"(instrument or other_source, not NARROWER or BROADER): a label is picked from "
                              f"the forms a source uses for this concept. Nothing was written.")
            if form["alias"] != new:
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: form {from_form} reads {form['alias']!r}, not {new!r}: a label "
                              f"picked from a form is that form's text. Nothing was written.")
        elif from_observation is not None:
            obs = conn.execute("SELECT observation_id, ref_id, surface_form, language "
                               "FROM observed_terms WHERE observation_id = ?",
                               (from_observation,)).fetchone()
            if obs is None:
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: observation {from_observation}: no such "
                              f"observed term.")
            if not _names_term(conn, from_observation, term_id):
                raise Refusal(
                    f"{_not_named_msg(conn, 'rename-term', from_observation, term_id)} "
                    f"If the source's phrase does name THIS concept, judge it: db.py adjudicate-term "
                    f"--observation-id {from_observation} --outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {term_id} "
                    f"--rationale ... --session ... (a later adjudication is the standing one), then rename "
                    f"from it. Nothing was written.")
            if not _retrieval_log().phrase_in_quote(new, obs["surface_form"]):
                raise Refusal(
                    f"rename-term: {new!r} is not in the observed phrase "
                    f"{obs['surface_form']!r}. A name taken from a source is the source's "
                    f"words. Nothing was written.")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        pick = {"term_id": term_id, "former_label": old, "form_id": from_form,
                "observation_id": from_observation,
                "ruling_quote": ruling_quote.strip() if ruling_quote else None,
                "judge": judge, "reason": reason}
        pick.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_label_picks", session))
        pick_id = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_label_picks ({','.join(pick)}) "
                               f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(pick))})", list(pick.values())).lastrowid
        sets = {"canonical_en": new}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "terms", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE terms SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE term_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [term_id])
        return {"term_id": term_id, "was": old, "now": new, "pick_id": pick_id, "judge": judge,
                "changed": True, "dry_run": dry_run}

                            pick of the name shown when several English instruments name the
                            concept differently (T-028; OD-38, owner 2026-11-12: "First recorded,
                            until a named judge picks; the pick is recorded with its reason");
      --from-observation N  the new name comes from a phrase a source USES, in the
                            source's own language (owner E1, 2026-11-06: a concept first
                            met outside English is named by that phrase), whose latest adjudication names
                            THIS term, whose surface form
                            contains the new name (the 2026-09-09 rule, kept by the owner
                            on 2026-10-09: names come from observed phrases);
      --ruling-quote "..."  or from the owner's own words, quoted verbatim and found
                            exactly once in references/project-standards.md, containing
                            the new name.
    Every route names its --judge (who picked) beside the --reason (OD-38).

    Nothing else moves: parameters, adjudications and extractions point at term_id, so the
    name is reached, never copied (rule 5). The label is not a form (OD-03), so the former
    label is NOT written into term_aliases and no AMENDED trailer is appended to scope_note
    (the owner's schema-shape statement of 2026-11-06: a correction appended to a note is a fact
    in the wrong cell): one term_label_picks row holds the former label, the route's one pointer,
    the judge and the reason. No other term may hold the new name, as a label or as an attested
    English form (_name_holder); a seed never refuses (E4).

    REFUSES: no judge; neither or several warrants; a value-bearing name (_VALUE_BEARING, as
    add-term); a quote not exactly once in the ledger or not containing the name; an observation
    whose latest adjudication does not name this term, or that does not contain the name; a form
    that is not an attested member form of this term or whose text is not the name; a name another
    term holds.

    new = (canonical_en or "").strip()
    if not new:
        raise Refusal("rename-term: --canonical-en is required: a term is its name.")
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(reason, term_id)
    judge = (judge or "").strip()
    if not judge:
        raise Refusal("rename-term: --judge is required: who picked this label (OD-38, owner 2026-11-12: "
                      "the pick is recorded with its reason, and a pick names its judge). Nothing was written.")
    if (from_observation is not None) + bool((ruling_quote or "").strip()) + (from_form is not None) != 1:
        raise Refusal(
            "rename-term: give exactly one warrant for the new name -- --from-form F (an attested "
            "form of this term), --from-observation N (a phrase an admitted source uses) or "
            "--ruling-quote '<the owner's words>' (found once in references/project-standards.md). "
            "A name with no warrant is a name typed by hand, which the 2026-09-09 rule forbids.")
    vb = _VALUE_BEARING_NAME.search(new)
    if vb:
        raise Refusal(
            f"rename-term: {new!r} carries a number, a comparator or a min/max word "
            f"({vb.group(0)!r}), so it "
            f"states a determination in its own name -- the item-layer defect "
            f"(DR-2026-08-19 section 1.1). Name the quantity, never its value.")
    if ruling_quote:
        dbcore.require_ledger_quote_once(ruling_quote, "rename-term: the --ruling-quote",
                                         "That ties this rename to one ruling.")
        if new.lower() not in dbcore.normalise_quote_text(ruling_quote).lower():
            raise Refusal(f"rename-term: the quoted ruling does not contain {new!r}; the "
                          f"words that authorise a name must say it.")

                            "WHERE term_id = ?", (term_id,)).fetchone()

        old = term["canonical_en"]
        if old == new:
            return {"term_id": term_id, "changed": False, "dry_run": dry_run}
        for clash in _name_holder(conn, new, "EN", exclude_term=term_id)["clashes"]:
            if clash["kind"] == "label":
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: {new!r} is already the name of {clash['term_id']}. "
                              f"Two terms with one name are one concept twice; that is a merge, "
                              f"not a rename. Nothing was written.")
            raise Refusal(f"rename-term: {new!r} is an alias ({clash['detail']}, form {clash['form_id']}) of "
                          f"{clash['term_id']}, attested. A name another term answers to would make "
                          f"one phrase point at two concepts. Nothing was written.")
        if from_form is not None:
            form = conn.execute("SELECT form_id, alias, alias_type, attestation FROM term_aliases "
                                "WHERE form_id = ? AND term_id = ?", (from_form, term_id)).fetchone()
            if (form is None or form["attestation"] not in dbcore.ATTESTED_FORMS
                    or form["alias_type"] in ("NARROWER", "BROADER")):
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: form {from_form} is not an attested member form of {term_id} "
                              f"(instrument or other_source, not NARROWER or BROADER): a label is picked from "
                              f"the forms a source uses for this concept. Nothing was written.")
            if form["alias"] != new:
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: form {from_form} reads {form['alias']!r}, not {new!r}: a label "
                              f"picked from a form is that form's text. Nothing was written.")

            obs = conn.execute("SELECT observation_id, ref_id, surface_form, language "
                               "FROM observed_terms WHERE observation_id = ?",
                               (from_observation,)).fetchone()
            if obs is None:
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: observation {from_observation}: no such "
                              f"observed term.")
            if not _names_term(conn, from_observation, term_id):
                raise Refusal(
                    f"{_not_named_msg(conn, 'rename-term', from_observation, term_id)} "
                    f"If the source's phrase does name THIS concept, judge it: db.py adjudicate-term "
                    f"--observation-id {from_observation} --outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {term_id} "
                    f"--rationale ... --session ... (a later adjudication is the standing one), then rename "
                    f"from it. Nothing was written.")
            if not _retrieval_log().phrase_in_quote(new, obs["surface_form"]):
                raise Refusal(
                    f"rename-term: {new!r} is not in the observed phrase "
                    f"{obs['surface_form']!r}. A name taken from a source is the source's "
                    f"words. Nothing was written.")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        pick = {"term_id": term_id, "former_label": old, "form_id": from_form,
                "observation_id": from_observation,
                "ruling_quote": ruling_quote.strip() if ruling_quote else None,
                "judge": judge, "reason": reason}
        pick.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_label_picks", session))
        pick_id = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_label_picks ({','.join(pick)}) "
                               f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(pick))})", list(pick.values())).lastrowid
        sets = {"canonical_en": new}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "terms", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE terms SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE term_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [term_id])
        return {"term_id": term_id, "was": old, "now": new, "pick_id": pick_id, "judge": judge,
                "changed": True, "dry_run": dry_run}

content.content:
## 1. base — read before touching a source
The catalogue every source is read against: `base_parameters` + `terms`/`term_aliases`, the lenses
(`base_taxonomy_identity`, `access_needs`, `base_icf`),
`slugs`, `lang_jur_map`. Codes AND names; no bare axis codes or population umbrellas.
- **Equivalence before minting.** Search terms and aliases first. A phrase a source uses for a term we hold is an
  alias, reached only through the chain `observe-term` (its `--context-quote` must be found byte-for-byte in a file
  saved for the source: a `scripts/research/full_text.py` derivation or the fetched page) → `adjudicate-term
  --outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id` → `add-alias --alias-type` (from the CHECK; it writes `attestation`, `other_source`
  unless `--attestation instrument`). A form read where no observation exists takes the base route (`add-alias --alias
  --language --jurisdiction --source-url --source-page|--source-clause --attestation`; the pair must be in `lang_jur_map`);
  a search aid with no locator takes `--seed owner_supplied --approval-ref '<ledger heading naming it>'` and is never vocabulary (`--seed model_seed` is refused, OR-17). A search names the forms it
  fired with `log-search --form-id`. A comparator ("not steeper than")
  or a value is not a name for the concept: adjudicate it `NOT-OURS`. The name rule is the writer's own: `add-term
  --canonical-en` and `rename-term --canonical-en` refuse a name carrying a digit, a comparison symbol, a `min` or
  `max` word, or a comparator word (`than`, `at least`, `at most`, `no more`, `no less`, `no fewer`, `no greater`,
  `not exceeding`, `exceed`); a definition is checked for digits, symbols and `min`/`max` only, because a definition is
  ordinary English. A duplicate parameter → `merge-parameter`; otherwise a new concept.
- **A new concept arises while a source is in hand** (`observe-term` needs `--ref-id` and a persisted quote), so base
  is re-entered from stages 3–4. **Claude never generates a phrase, name or alias** (OR-17): it is the source's own
  wording, present in its jurisdiction and language. `add-term --from-observation` mints the term and its NAMES-NEW
  adjudication together; it refuses a near match (shared tokens with a term or an alias that is not a `model_seed`) unless `--distinct-from
  TERM-ID` names it and the rationale says why. `adjudicate-term` never writes NAMES-NEW. Owner approval is the data
  PR the owner reads (OR-17: "bulk, with me reading the PR"); `add-parameter` and `decline-parameter` take no
  approval flag; `--approval-ref` is the flag of the verbs that record an approval (derive them: `grep -n -F -- '"--approval-ref"' scripts/db.py`). `add-parameter` takes instead `--quantity-kind` and `--quantity-kind-observation-id` (T-020): the kind of quantity, from `base_quantity_kinds`, and the observation whose quote states a value of it.
- `set-parameter-direction --ref-id` records which way is better **from an admitted source** that holds an
  extraction for the parameter (ledger 2026-10-30, ACTION 6; stored in `base_parameters.direction_ref_id`); a
  direction with no source is refused. Without a direction stage 6 cannot select a value and says so in its gap. A
  direction set before that rule carries no source (derive: `SELECT parameter_id FROM base_parameters WHERE
  accessibility_direction IS NOT NULL AND direction_ref_id IS NULL`): it stands as history, and whether it is
  backfilled, and whether `contested` takes a source, are open owner question 7 of the 2026-11-06 round-3 adjudication.
- Checks: `scripts/validate_parameters.py`, `scripts/audit/schema_reference_audit.py`,
  `scripts/audit/identifier_floor_audit.py`.

## 2. research — by topic, across languages and jurisdictions *(skipped by `from-evidence`)*
- Coverage is slug × bucket member, bounded by Scope above. In-language terms come from `term_aliases` and the source's
  own words (R11); never from memory or back-translation. Co-1 / T2 / Co-2 first (R1). Skills: `multilingual-research`,
  `functional-deficit-researcher`, `research-log-manager`.
- **Log every query before screening:** `log-search --prior-expectation … --slug … --language … --jurisdiction …`
  (R8). A search names what it looked for (`--slug`, `--parameter` or `--mined-ref-id`); `--slug` must exist and
  `--parameter` must be active. `--language` is a two-letter code from `lang_jur_map` (derive: `SELECT DISTINCT
     --prior-expectation '<what you expect and why, written before you run it>' \   # refused without it (R8)
     --slug {slug} \                   # omit for a search made for one parameter (--parameter {parameter_id}) or one source (--mined-ref-id); a search naming none is refused
     --language {lang_code} \
     --jurisdiction {jur_code} \        # omit if the search was not jurisdiction-scoped
     --identity {identity_code} --icf {icf_code} --needs {need_code} \   # the lens this query covered; each optional and checked against its registry
     --query-text '{the query, exactly as fired}' \
     --form-id {rowid} --form-id {rowid} \   # repeatable: the rowid of each term_aliases row this query fired (select rowid, term_id, alias, language from term_aliases); stored by the form's key; a form's language must be the search's --language. --terms-used is refused
     --engine {pubmed|crossref|web|...} \
     --depth-method {scoping|systematic} \             # only two; a citation chase is --mining-direction
     --target-tier {1..6} --target-evidence-type {co1|clinical|code|...} \
     --results-found {N} --results-screened {N} --results-admitted {N} \
     --admitted-ref-id REF-NNNNN \      # repeatable; writes the admission junction too
     --session {session_stem}
      - {file: scripts/db.py, func: observe_term, needle: "_refuse_tombstone"}
  - id: M03.t2
    from: "OBSERVED"
    to: "ADJUDICATED-*"
    via: "db.py adjudicate-term"
    guards:
      - "a rationale is required; NAMES-* needs a term_id that exists; NOT-OURS and DEFERRED must carry none"
      - "divergent adjudications are DELIBERATELY allowed (no uniqueness on observation_id) -- a contest, not an error"
    evidence:
      - {file: scripts/db.py, func: adjudicate_term, needle: "Divergent adjudications are DELIBERATELY permitted"}
      - {file: scripts/db.py, func: adjudicate_term, needle: "names a term, so --term-id is required"}
  - id: M03.t3
    from: "OBSERVED"
    to: "TERM + ADJUDICATED-NAMES-NEW (one act)"
    via: "db.py add-term --from-observation"
    guards:
      - "a canonical name carrying a digit, comparator or min/max word is refused (the container may not state its answer)"
      - "a name that already exists is refused and pointed at NAMES-EXISTING"
      - "a term can only be minted FROM an observation"
    evidence:
      - {file: scripts/db.py, func: insert_term, needle: "states a determination in its own name"}
      - {file: scripts/db.py, func: insert_term, needle: "That makes this NAMES-EXISTING"}
  - id: M03.t4
    from: "TERM"
    to: "PARAMETER-ACTIVE"
    via: "db.py add-parameter"

and are never used to rank populations. Identity profiles (Deaf community;
identity-model neurodivergence) carry **no** ICD anchor by design.

**Naming.** Person-first vs identity-first conventions differ *between communities
and between languages*; the taxonomy defers to each community's stated preference
in English and to native-language conventions via `term_aliases` — display names
are presentation-layer, revisable without schema change **[T1][T5]**.

new='''def insert_term(from_observation: int, canonical_en: str, rationale: str, session: str,
                definition: str = None, domain: str = None, scope_note: str = None,
                dry_run: bool = False, distinct_from: list = None, attestation: str = None,
                *, first_form: str = None, form_language: str = None,
                form_jurisdiction: str = None, source_url: str = None, source_page: str = None,
                source_line: int = None, source_clause: str = None, usage_type: str = None):
    """Mint a term for a concept new to the vocabulary, with its FIRST FORM, in one act.

    The missing half of D-0173. `adjudicate-term --outcome NAMES-NEW` refuses unless the
    term already exists, and nothing created one. A checker whose satisfying writer does not
    exist is a trap (CLAUDE.md section 8).

    A concept is its term_id; its names are forms in term_aliases; canonical_en is OUR English
    descriptive label (OD-03, T-028). Two routes, exactly one:
      from_observation  the observed phrase is the first member row (pointing at the
                        observation), and the term is adjudicated NAMES-NEW from it -- one
                        judgement: *this phrase names a concept we did not hold*;
      first_form        the base route (seventh statement, 2026-11-06): the form with its own
                        locator (source_url and a page or clause), language and jurisdiction.
    `attestation` (instrument | other_source) is said, never inferred. The label must sit
    inside the phrase when the phrase is English (the 2026-09-09 rule, kept 2026-10-09); a
    concept first met in another language takes an English descriptive label (eighth
    statement), which v_term_names marks as ours.

    REFUSES: no label, no rationale, a value-bearing label; neither or both routes; an
    attestation that is not one; an English phrase not containing the label; a label another
    term holds; a form another concept holds, attested, in that language, unless named by
    --distinct-from (a recorded conflation); a near match not named by --distinct-from; on the
    base route a (language, jurisdiction) pair lang_jur_map lacks, or no locator.
    """
    canonical_en = (canonical_en or "").strip()
    rationale = (rationale or "").strip()
    if not canonical_en:
        raise Refusal("--canonical-en is required: our English label for the concept.")
    if not rationale:
        raise Refusal(
            "--rationale is required. Minting a term is an adjudication, and an "
            "adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested.")
    vb = _VALUE_BEARING_NAME.search(canonical_en)
    if vb:
        raise Refusal(
            f"--canonical-en {canonical_en!r} REFUSED: it carries a number, a comparator "
            f"or a min/max word ({vb.group(0)!r}), so it states a determination in its own name.\\n"
            f"That is the defect the item layer was deleted for -- a container that "
            f"announces its answer predisposes every finding filed into it "
            f"(DR-2026-08-19 §1.1: 42 of 93 item names embedded a determination).\\n"
            f"Name the PARAMETER, not the value: 'corridor width', not "
            f"'corridor width >=1200 mm'. The value belongs in the determination.")
    if (from_observation is None) == (first_form is None):
        raise Refusal("add-term: give exactly one route: --from-observation N (an observed "
                      "phrase) or --first-form with its language, jurisdiction and locator.")
    if attestation not in _ATTESTED:
        raise Refusal(f"add-term: --attestation {'|'.join(_ATTESTED)} is required: whether the "
                      f"first form's source is an instrument is said, never inferred.")
    distinct = set(distinct_from or [])
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        if usage_type is not None:
            dbcore.check_declared(conn, "term_aliases", "usage_type", usage_type,
                                  "add-term --usage-type")
        if from_observation is not None:
            obs = conn.execute("SELECT o.observation_id, o.surface_form, o.ref_id, o.language, "
                               "e.jurisdiction FROM observed_terms o LEFT JOIN evidence_sources e "
                               "ON e.ref_id = o.ref_id WHERE o.observation_id=?",
                               [from_observation]).fetchone()
            if obs is None:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"observation {from_observation}: no such observed term. A term is minted "
                    f"FROM an observed phrase (db.py observe-term), never from nothing -- that "
                    f"is what makes the vocabulary an output of the work rather than a "
                    f"presupposition.")
            form, lang, jur = obs["surface_form"], (obs["language"] or "EN").upper(), obs["jurisdiction"]
            locator = {"observation_id": from_observation}
        else:
            form, lang, jur = (first_form or "").strip(), (form_language or "").strip().upper(), \\
                form_jurisdiction
            if not form or not lang or not jur:
                raise Refusal("add-term --first-form needs --form-language and "
                              "--form-jurisdiction: whose instrument, in which language.")
            if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM lang_jur_map WHERE upper(language) = ? AND "
                                "jurisdiction = ?", (lang, jur)).fetchone():
                raise Refusal(f"add-term: ({lang}, {jur}) is not a pair lang_jur_map holds.")
            if not (source_url and (source_page or source_clause)):
                raise Refusal("add-term: a first form says where: --source-url and "
                              "--source-page or --source-clause (--source-line optional).")
            locator = {"source_url": source_url, "source_page": source_page,
                       "source_line": source_line, "source_clause": source_clause}
        if lang == "EN" and canonical_en.casefold() not in form.casefold():
            raise Refusal(
                f"--canonical-en {canonical_en!r} is not inside the observed phrase "
                f"{form!r}. A name is a phrase an admitted source uses, in its "
                f"own language (owner OR-17: the model may not coin names; ruling 2026-11-06, "
                f"E1). Use the phrase as written, or a contiguous part of it. Only a concept "
                f"first met outside English takes an English descriptive label of our own "
                f"(eighth statement, 2026-11-06).")
        clash = _label_clash(conn, canonical_en)
        if clash:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{canonical_en!r} is already TERM {clash['term_id']} "
                f"({clash['detail']!r}). That makes this NAMES-EXISTING, not "
                f"NAMES-NEW:\\n  db.py adjudicate-term --observation-id {from_observation} "
                f"--outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {clash['term_id']} --rationale ...")
        held = [c for c in _name_holder(conn, form, lang)["clashes"]
                if c["term_id"] not in distinct]
        if held:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{form!r} ({lang}) is already an attested form of " +
                ", ".join(c["term_id"] for c in held) + ". If it names that concept, "
                "adjudicate NAMES-EXISTING; if one phrase names two concepts, record the "
                "conflation with --distinct-from " + " --distinct-from ".join(
                    c["term_id"] for c in held) + " and say why in --rationale. Nothing was written.")
        near = _near_terms(conn, canonical_en, "EN")
        if lang != "EN":
            near += _near_terms(conn, form, lang)
        near = [(t, h) for t, h in near if t not in distinct]
        if near:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{canonical_en!r} is a near match of " +
                "; ".join(f"{t} {h!r}" for t, h in near[:5]) +
                ". Equivalence before minting: if it names one of these, adjudicate "
                "NAMES-EXISTING (a narrower or broader phrase is an alias: add-alias "
                "--alias-type NARROWER/BROADER); if it is a distinct concept, say so with "
                "--distinct-from " + " --distinct-from ".join(t for t, _ in near[:5]) +
                " and the --rationale must say why. Nothing was written.")
        term_id = _mint_term_id(conn)
        row = {"term_id": term_id, "canonical_en": canonical_en,
               "definition": definition, "domain": domain, "scope_note": scope_note}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "terms", session))
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO terms ({','.join(row)}) "
                     f"VALUES ({','.join('?'*len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        out = {"term_id": term_id, "canonical_en": canonical_en, "first_form": form,
               "form_language": lang, "dry_run": dry_run}
        if from_observation is not None:
            adj = {"observation_id": from_observation, "outcome": "NAMES-NEW",
                   "term_id": term_id, "rationale": rationale}
            adj.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_adjudications", session))
            cur = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_adjudications ({','.join(adj)}) "
                               f"VALUES ({','.join('?'*len(adj))})", list(adj.values()))
            out.update(adjudication_id=cur.lastrowid, from_ref_id=obs["ref_id"])
        frow = {"term_id": term_id, "alias": form, "language": _alias_language(conn, lang),
                "alias_type": "SYNONYM", "jurisdiction": jur, "attestation": attestation,
                "usage_type": usage_type,
                "notes": rationale if from_observation is None else None, **locator}
        frow.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_aliases", session))
        try:
            cur = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_aliases ({','.join(frow)}) "
                               f"VALUES ({','.join('?'*len(frow))})", list(frow.values()))
        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:

                          f"written.")

Given in the session `session_2026-11-16-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMfdrQNV9XzGP4dyZm), in four typed messages while the second tooling stack was being built, the first after the coordinator reported that `term_label_picks.observation_id` and the warrant keys of `term_relations` point from base tables into the evidence stage, the third after the coordinator put the two questions of the term-name view (the sweep list of `session_2026-11-18-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack-2`) to the owner, and the fourth in answer to the coordinator's one question whether a base row may keep a source's `ref_id`. Server-clock times were not captured; derive them from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "absorbed by base and grounded" -- transcripts`).

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "then the base grounds itself except for when evidence that allows for new terms/aliases/parameters to be found is pointed to as justification"
>
> "but this justification should then be absorbed by base and grounded as if it were always there to prevent loops/recursion/sequencing conflicts"
>
> "likely have to do a convergence test for number of term appearances for concept or I rule"
>
> "ref_id as provenance? sure. but it's ONLY for provenance"

**Readings.**

- [ASSUMPTION: OD-71. A base row (a term, a form of it, a parameter, a relation, a label pick) may cite the evidence row (an observation, a source, an extraction) that allowed the item to be found, as its justification; that is the exception to "the base grounds itself" (2026-11-06, seventh statement) — basis: the first sentence].
- [ASSUMPTION: OD-71. "absorbed by base and grounded as if it were always there" means the base keeps the justification in its OWN columns (what was found and where: the form, its language and jurisdiction, the source's URL, page and line, and the quoted words), so the base row reads, checks and orders without any evidence row, and nothing in the base waits on that evidence being admitted, adjudicated or verified, or is sequenced after it; the evidence stage keeps its own judgment, tier and verification of the source, which the base does not hold — basis: the second sentence and its stated purpose, "to prevent loops/recursion/sequencing conflicts"; this keeps CLAUDE.md rule 5 (a fact in one home) where it can: where a form was found is the base's fact, the source's standing is the evidence stage's].
- [ASSUMPTION: OD-71. A base row may keep the source's `ref_id` (or an observation id) beside the absorbed grounding, and that is ONLY provenance: nothing in the base validates against it, orders after it, joins through it to decide a state, or waits on it; a base writer neither requires it nor refuses a row for lacking it — basis: "ref_id as provenance? sure. but it's ONLY for provenance"]. The wording of the owner's second statement on whether the quoted words are repeated in the base row (or only the locator) is NOT stated and is not read in.
- [ASSUMPTION: OD-72. "number of term appearances for concept" means the number of occurrences of a form among a concept's forms (the rows of `term_aliases`, one per occurrence since migration 146), and "a convergence test" means the displayed name is the form whose appearances converge, and "or I rule" means the owner may set the name by a named judge's pick as OD-38 already provides — basis: the words; "likely" marks a direction, not a settled rule].
- OD-72 is a DIRECTION, not a decision: "likely have to do". It moves OD-38's "first recorded" (2026-11-12, fifth set) toward a count of appearances; it does not withdraw OD-38's "until a named judge picks; the pick is recorded with its reason".

OD-71: the base grounds itself; evidence that allowed a new term, form or parameter is absorbed into the base's own columns
OD-71 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

OD-72: displayed name by a convergence test on the appearances of a form for a concept, or the owner's ruling; the test is not specified
OD-72 STATUS: REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER

**What it does.**

- **OD-71.** A base table holds no foreign key into the evidence stage and no pointer that a base row's validity waits on. Where a base row is justified by evidence, the justification is written into the base row's own cells. Sequencing runs one way only: evidence may be found and named from the base; the base is never ordered after evidence. It reaches `term_label_picks.observation_id` and `add-term --from-observation`'s hold of a form `unrecorded` until a quote verifies (T-028), the warrant keys of `term_relations` (T-029), `term_aliases`' own source columns, and any later base table that carries a warrant.
- **OD-72.** The displayed name of a concept stops reading "first recorded" and reads a count of appearances, unless a named judge has picked; the owner is to specify the test.

**What it does not decide.** OD-71: whether the absorbed grounding repeats the quoted words or only the locator; how an existing pointer is migrated. OD-72: what counts as an appearance (a row of `term_aliases`; a row per language and jurisdiction; a source), the tolerance of the convergence, the tie, a concept with no form, and how "a concept first met outside English" is decided (the second question of the sweep list).

-- 150_label_picks_ground_in_base.sql
-- SCHEMA migration, compensating 146 (T-028 repair; owner statements 2026-11-18, OD-71: "the base grounds itself
-- except for when evidence that allows for new terms/aliases/parameters to be found is pointed to as justification;
-- but this justification should then be absorbed by base and grounded as if it were always there", and "ref_id as
-- provenance? sure. but it's ONLY for provenance"). No data rows.
--
-- term_label_picks (a base table) carried `observation_id REFERENCES observed_terms`, a foreign key into the evidence
-- stage. It is rebuilt without it. A pick's warrant is the base's own: the named judge, the reason, and either the
-- form it rests on (a term_aliases row; rename-term --from-observation now rests on this term's form holding the
-- observed phrase) or the owner's quoted words. `ref_id` is PROVENANCE ONLY: nullable, no foreign key, validated
-- against nothing and read by no base decision.
-- Rows are copied as they stand; a row whose only warrant was an observation cannot be copied without a form, and the
-- CHECK then aborts the migration rather than drop it (none existed when this was written: `select count(*) from
-- term_label_picks where observation_id is not null`).

CREATE TABLE _150_term_label_picks (
    pick_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    former_label        TEXT,                                               -- NULL only for a mint by add-term --first-form
    form_id             INTEGER REFERENCES term_aliases(form_id),          -- the form the pick rests on
    ruling_quote        TEXT,                                               -- rename-term --ruling-quote
    ref_id              TEXT,                                               -- provenance only (OD-71): no foreign key
    judge               TEXT NOT NULL,                                      -- who picked
    reason              TEXT NOT NULL,                                      -- why (add-term --first-form: its --rationale)
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    CHECK ((form_id IS NOT NULL) + (ruling_quote IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK (former_label IS NOT NULL OR form_id IS NOT NULL)
);

INSERT INTO _150_term_label_picks (pick_id, term_id, former_label, form_id, ruling_quote, ref_id, judge, reason,
                                   created_at, created_by_session)
SELECT pick_id, term_id, former_label, form_id, ruling_quote, NULL, judge, reason, created_at, created_by_session
  FROM term_label_picks;

DROP TABLE term_label_picks;
ALTER TABLE _150_term_label_picks RENAME TO term_label_picks;
